nameStory: The "earwort" part of this plant's name comes from its tiny, ear-shaped leaves that grow in pairs along the stem, creating a distinctive pattern that early botanists thought resembled little ears. The "blunted" part refers to the rounded, obtuse tips of these leaves, which distinguish it from its sharp-pointed relatives. Like many bryophytes (mosses and liverworts), this little plant got a descriptive name that helps you remember its key identifying feature!
description: Blunted Earwort is a tiny liverwort that forms small, dark green patches on rocks and soil in shady, moist places. This diminutive plant grows as flat, creeping stems only about half an inch to an inch long, with pairs of overlapping leaves that create a braided or rope-like appearance. Unlike mosses, liverworts like this one have a flattened, leafy body that hugs close to whatever surface it's growing on. You'll need to look closely or use a hand lens to really appreciate its intricate structure, as individual plants are quite small.

idTips.label: Blunted leaf tips
idTips.description: The tiny leaves have distinctly rounded, blunt tips rather than sharp points - this is your best clue and requires close examination or a magnifying glass to see clearly

idTips.label: Two-ranked leaves
idTips.description: Leaves are arranged in two neat rows along the stem, overlapping like shingles on a roof, creating a flattened, braided appearance you can feel with your fingertip

idTips.label: Dark green coloration
idTips.description: The plant has a deep, rich green color that's often darker than surrounding mosses, sometimes with a slightly brownish tinge in older parts

idTips.label: Creeping growth habit
idTips.description: Forms low, flat patches that feel slightly rough to the touch and cling tightly to rock surfaces or soil, never growing upright like many mosses

idTips.label: Small size
idTips.description: Individual shoots are typically less than an inch long and create patches only a few inches across - much smaller than most mosses in similar habitats

habitat: Look for Blunted Earwort on damp, shaded rocks, particularly sandstone or acidic substrates in cool, humid locations throughout New England's forests. It favors spots that stay consistently moist but not waterlogged, often found on north-facing rock outcrops, stream banks, or in deeply shaded ravines. This species seems to prefer undisturbed, mature forest environments where humidity levels remain stable year-round.

seasonality.spring: Best time for identification as the plant is actively growing and showing its freshest green coloration. New growth makes the leaf arrangement most visible.
seasonality.summer: May become somewhat dormant and darker during dry periods, but still identifiable by its characteristic leaf shape and arrangement in consistently moist spots.
seasonality.fall: Often shows renewed growth as humidity increases and temperatures cool, making it easier to spot the distinctive blunted leaf tips.
seasonality.winter: Remains visible under snow in protected locations, though growth slows considerably. The persistent dark green color can help locate it during winter explorations.

funFact: This tiny plant is essentially a living fossil - liverworts like Blunted Earwort represent one of the earliest forms of complex life to colonize land over 400 million years ago, making them older than dinosaurs and even most insects!
confusionNotes: Most easily confused with small mosses or other liverworts, but the key is looking for that flat, two-ranked leaf arrangement rather than the spiraled leaves of mosses. Remember: "Blunted and braided" - the leaves look blunt-tipped and create a braided pattern along the stem, unlike the fuzzy, all-around leaf arrangement of mosses.
contextualKnowledge: The term "liverwort" comes from medieval times when people thought these plants resembled tiny livers and believed they could cure liver ailments - a concept called the "doctrine of signatures." Modern liverworts like this one are completely unrelated to medical treatments but remain fascinating examples of some of Earth's most ancient plant lineages.
compareHints: Blunted Earwort differs from its close relative Sharp-pointed Earwort mainly in the leaf tips - Sharp-pointed Earwort has distinctly pointed, acute leaf tips while Blunted Earwort's are rounded and obtuse. Both have the same two-ranked leaf arrangement and similar size, so you really need to examine the leaf tips closely with a hand lens. Sharp-pointed Earwort also tends to prefer slightly different microhabitats, often growing on more exposed rocks.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Sharp-pointed Earwort differs from Blunted Earwort primarily in its leaf tips - run your finger gently across them and you'll feel the sharp points versus the smooth, rounded tips of its relative.
